title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 426-428): Grothendieck is computing in a group of 'normalized' automorphisms u_ξ of the profinite fundamental group Π̂_{0,3}. This is a GT-like group, the 'Teichmüller-type' group M_{0,3}^{!~}, also written N_{0,3}^{!~}(0). Here Π̂_{0,3} is profinite free on loops l_0, l_1, l_∞ with l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1. The automorphism u_ξ is determined by a parameter ξ ∈ Π̂_{0,3} and an exponent μ, via u_ξ(ε_1) = int(ξ)(ε_1^μ). The element τ_∞, of order 2, is u_{ξ'} with ξ' = l_1^{-1}; it is the 'complex conjugation fixing ∞' and inverts l_1.

The proposition on the previous page states that the centralizer of τ in the group is {1, τ}. Writing out u_ξ u_{ξ'} = u_{ξ'} u_ξ with the composition law u_a u_b = u_{u_a(b)a} gives equation (62): ξ^{-1} τ_∞(ξ) = l_1^{1-μ} = l_1^{-2ν}, with μ = 1+2ν.

On this page:
(63) ξ = l_1^ν is a solution, since τ_∞(l_1^ν) = l_1^{-ν}.
Uniqueness: if ξ_0 is a second solution, then τ_∞(ξ ξ_0^{-1}) = ξ ξ_0^{-1}. So the solution is unique exactly when the fixed subgroup of τ_∞ on Π̂_{0,3} is trivial, which is (64): (Π̂_{0,3})^{τ_∞} = {1}. For the discrete free group this is elementary. Grothendieck admits that it extends to the profinite completion.
Finally ξ must satisfy the cocycle/normalization relation ξ ρ(ξ) ρ²(ξ) = 1, where ρ is the order-3 rotation permuting 0, 1, ∞. He asserts this forces the exponent to be such that u ∈ {1, τ_∞}, so the centralizer of τ_∞ is {1, τ_∞}.

The purpose is to show complex conjugation is self-centralizing in this GT-type group, the analogue of the classical fact for Gal(Q̄/Q). Next page: §48 starts constructing a group scheme via the map α ↦ α ρ(α)^{-1}.
errors: The conclusion 'ν = ±1' is inconsistent with the stated goal u ∈ {1, τ_∞}. The identity corresponds to ξ = 1, i.e. ν = 0, μ = 1. τ_∞ corresponds to ξ = l_1^{-1}, i.e. ν = -1, μ = -1. So the correct statement is μ = ±1, equivalently ν ∈ {0, -1}. With ρ(l_1) = l_0 and ρ²(l_1) = l_∞, one checks l_1^ν l_0^ν l_∞^ν = 1 exactly for ν = 0 or -1 in the discrete group. Probably a slip of ν for μ.

'On voit de suite' is a gap in the profinite setting, where ν ∈ Ẑ. Abelianization gives no information, since l_0 + l_1 + l_∞ = 0. Showing l_1^ν ρ(l_1^ν) ρ²(l_1^ν) = 1 only for ν ∈ {0, -1} needs a non-abelian (e.g. metabelian or finite-quotient) argument.

(64) is only assumed ('si on admet que les résultats discrets se prolongent au cas profini'). It is true. F̂_2 ⋊ ⟨τ⟩ is the profinite completion of a free product of three copies of Z/2, and a free factor in a free profinite product is self-centralizing (Herfort–Ribes). But this was not proved on the page.

ideas.what: Centralizer of the complex-conjugation-type involution τ_∞ in the GT-like automorphism group of Π̂_{0,3} is {1, τ_∞}
ideas.modern_name: self-centralizing property of complex conjugation in (a variant of) the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Analogue of the Artin–Schreier-type fact for Gal(Q̄/Q). For GT̂, involutions were studied by Lochak–Schneps (1990s); I am unsure whether the centralizer statement is explicitly published.

ideas.what: Reduction of the commutation equation to a twisted-fixed-point equation ξ^{-1}τ(ξ) = l_1^{-2ν}, with uniqueness ⇔ trivial fixed subgroup of τ on Π̂
ideas.modern_name: nonabelian H^1 / twisted conjugacy for an involution acting on a profinite free group

ideas.what: Fixed points of complex conjugation on the profinite free group π̂_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}) are trivial
ideas.modern_name: centralizers of torsion in free profinite products

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly leaves as an assumption that the discrete fact (fixed points of τ_∞ on Π_{0,3} trivial) extends to the profinite completion. This later became a theorem in profinite combinatorial group theory, a link he anticipates but does not prove.
missed.quote: si on admet que les résultats discrets se prolongent au cas profini, de façon à avoir (64) (Π̂_{0,3})^{τ_∞} = {1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Shows Grothendieck needing Herfort–Ribes-type results for the anabelian/GT program. Minor historically; the result is now known.

missed.claim: An (incomplete) proof that complex conjugation is self-centralizing in his version of the Teichmüller-type group acting on Π̂_{0,3}.
missed.quote: on voit de suite que cela implique ν = ±1, i.e. u ∈ {1, τ_∞}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A GT̂-analogue of a classical Galois-theoretic property. Possibly folklore, but an early explicit derivation.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, early computation of the centralizer of complex conjugation in a GT-type group, explicitly flagging the profinite fixed-point issue. It is close to known results (Lochak–Schneps on involutions, Herfort–Ribes on centralizers) and contains a sign/letter slip, so it is only mildly notable.
transcription_corrections: Last line: the written 'ν = ±1' should mathematically read μ = ±1 (ν ∈ {0, -1}). The image seems to show 'ν = ±1', so this is Grothendieck's slip, not a transcription error.
'cette solution est unique [-?-]': in the image a crossed-out word precedes 'si on admet'.
'(car τ_∞(l_1) = l_1^{-1} donc τ_∞(ξ) = l_1^{-ν})' is correctly read.
